{{Quote|Gungans from every city across the swamps stood ear to ear. Otoh Mandassa with Otoh Gunga, Oxon City with Umberbool City.|[[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]], about the Battle of Naboo|audio=GunganCities.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
'''Oxon City''', also known as '''Oxon''', was a [[City/Legends|city]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in which [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] and [[Human/Legends|Humans]] lived. During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the city was surrounded and advanced upon by the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|forces]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. Later, the Gungans of Oxon City contributed forces to the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Jamillia/Legends|Jamillia]] of Naboo designated the city as one of several [[Refugee/Legends|refugee]] arrival stations on the world.

==Description==
{{Quote|&hellip;Naboo has designated a number of slips in their ports of Theed, Oxon and Kwilaan as refugee arrival stations, even at the expense of moving commercial mining ventures to limited service ports.|A HoloNet report on Naboo's increased intake of refugees|<ref name="HNN52" />}}
Oxon City,<ref name="GB" /> also shortened to Oxon,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> was a [[City/Legends|city]] in the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], inhabited by both the [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]]<ref name="GB" /> and the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]]. It was considered one of the principal Human settlements on the world,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and was located to the southeast of the city of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the Human [[Capital/Legends|capital]], and [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]], which contained the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] Gungan capital, [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]].<ref name="Secrets" /> Oxon City contained a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]].<ref name="HNN52" />

==History==
{{Quote|Our world is generous with uninhabited lands that we are willing to share in this time of upheaval. Together, the Naboo and the Gungans will open Naboo's plentiful spaces as a new home for those in need.|Queen Jamillia|<ref name="HNN52" />}}
During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="GB" /> the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] landed three [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing crafts]] in a triangular formation in the vicinity of Oxon. The crafts then deployed their units of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droids]], isolating the city and confusing any potential defenders. The droids then advanced on Oxon City before moving on to [[Capture of Theed/Legends|capture]] Theed.<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile|22|LAN 1-2|Trade Federation C-9979 Landing Ship}}</ref>

[[File:Gunganarmy.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Gungans from Oxon City fought on the Great Grass Plains in the Battle of Naboo.]]
Later in the invasion, Oxon City contributed [[Militiagung/Legends|Gungan warriors]] to the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]], who fought alongside their [[Gungan society|brethren]] from [[Otoh Mandassa]], [[Umberbool City]], and Otoh Gunga to repel the invading [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|forces]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] at the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].<ref name="GB" /> After the planet's freedom was won in the battle, Gungans began the construction of a [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] on the Naboo [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. A [[Starship/Legends|shipment]] of machine parts was hijacked by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] on its way from Oxon to the moon installation, prompting the [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House of Naboo]] to assign a group of [[Echo Flight]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] to escort further shipments.<ref name="TST">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=starfighter_stats|text="The Starfighter Trap" Character Statistics}}</ref>

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name=HNN52Date">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|regional/13418_1.html|Mid Rim Worlds Open Ports to Refugees}} is set on the date 13:4:18, which corresponds to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] according to the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Jamillia/Legends|Jamillia]] of Naboo loosened the planet's immigration restrictions and designated spaceports in Oxon, Theed, and [[Kwilaan Starport/Legends|Kwilaan Starport]] as [[Refugee/Legends|refugee]] arrival stations. Her decision came at the cost of moving commercial [[Mining/Legends|mining]] ventures to specific service ports. Jamillia's announcement was reported in a 13:4:18 issue of the [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition|CoCo District Edition]] of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="HNN52" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|&hellip;marching on the city of Oxon. There is no resistance.|OOM-9, reporting his progress to the Neimoidians|<ref name="Insiders">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref>}}
[[File:OOMNineOrders.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Oxon City originated in a draft of ''The Phantom Menace'', in a scene where OOM-9 reported on its invasion to his Neimoidian superiors.]]
The city of Oxon originated in the revised second draft of the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] by [[George Lucas]],<ref name="Insiders" /> but did not appear in the finished film,<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> which was released on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> The draft was included in the [[Wikipedia:CD-ROM|CD-ROM]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide]]'',<ref name="Insiders" /> released on [[June 23]], 1999.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19990623.html|text=''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''Insider's Guide''}}</ref> In the draft, in a scene set during the Trade Federation's landing on Naboo, the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] reports to the Trade Federation's [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] leadership that the Droid Army is marching on the city to no resistance.<ref name="Insiders" />

Oxon was then first mentioned canonically with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity in [[Steve Miller]]'s short story, "[[The Starfighter Trap]]," when it was published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 1|first issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Gamer">{{GamerCite|1|The Starfighter Trap}}</ref> in [[November]] [[2000]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars Gamer Special Edition]]''</ref> The city is referenced by the character [[Rhys Dallows]] in a line of dialogue where he mentions encountering a [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo]] [[Purchasing Agent]] in Oxon.<ref name="Gamer" /> Before being published in ''Star Wars Gamer 1'', "The Starfighter Trap" had been published in three parts online, with the first part appearing on [[StarWars.com]] on [[October 27]], [[2000]]. In that version of the story, the line featuring the reference to Oxon instead referred to the city of [[Keren/Legends|Keren]].<ref name="StarWarsStarfighterTrap">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/f20001027|text=The Starfighter Trap}}</ref>

It was further identified as Oxon City in the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.<ref name="GB" /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', released in [[2008]], stated that Oxon was a human settlement,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> despite its prior portrayals as a Gungan habitation and the established animosity between them until the Invasion of Naboo.<ref name="GB" />
